text:
sam: Quick question — we're rolling a terraform change to switch service X to NLB with TLS passthrough + a fallback path to ALB. Wanted to check implications for cert wiring and secret scope. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2142
li: quick context: original was ALB terminate, now intent is NLB passthrough for latency-sensitive routes, ALB as fallback for legacy clients
sam: yeah, exactly. Plan is: primary NLB (TLS passthrough) -> pods, fallback ALB (TLS terminate) -> same svc. We were planning to attach cert via k8s secret mounted to ingress/ALB, but NLB passthrough needs cert on pod or use SNI routing to a target proxy — confused about the least-effort approach
endri: NLB passthrough doesn't terminate TLS. If you want TLS offload on ALB only, you can keep pod side with plain http and let ALB terminate. But for end-to-end TLS (NLB passthrough) you need cert on pods (or use sidecar that handles TLS).
li: another option: use TLS protocol at NLB and use target type 'instance' or 'ip' with TLS listener + set proxy protocol? AWS NLB can do TCP/TLS passthrough but it doesn't manage certs. For SNI-based routing you need aws-lb-controller + multiple listeners and then forward to ALB? messy
oliver: fwiw we have a small helper in infra that syncs AWS cert ARNs into k8s secrets for ALB. Not used for NLB. See docs: https://internal.redwood/docs/aws-lb-controller-cert-sync
sam: thanks. Two practical asks: 1) can we keep minimal terraform changes so PR is small? 2) what's the recommended secret binding pattern so ALB and pods (if needed) can both use same cert without duplicating rotation effort
natalie: for (2) we usually store cert ARN in Vault and have a controller sync the active pem into a namespace secret named tls/cert-<env>. ALB controller reads the cert via annotation (uses ARN) and k8s workloads mount the secret if they need TLS. That way rotation is one source.
endri: exact terraform diff: add aws_lb (NLB) resource + change service annotations. But I would avoid creating a second cert secret in multiple namespaces. Use a shared "infra-cert" namespace secret and RBAC to allow mount where necessary.
sam: sample service annotations I'm testing: ```yaml
metadata:
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb-ip"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-cert: "arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:123456789012:certificate/abcd"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-ssl-ports: "443"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
```
li: that looks OK for TCP passthrough if you want NLB to handle TLS listener but note: ssl-cert annotation is for classic/ALB in some controllers. aws-load-balancer-controller expects Ingress resources for ALB TLS. For NLB you might need to create aws_lb_listener resource in terraform to attach cert.
infra-bot: plan started by @sam on infra/terraform-modules/services (run-id: 4c2f) — no changes to secrets yet, creating aws_lb and aws_lb_target_group resources
sam: infra-bot thx. Plan shows NLB + listener with certificate ARN — so cert still referenced in terraform. That means rotation will require terraform apply unless we switch to Vault sync approach
natalie: we should avoid hardcoding ARN in tf module. Use var.cert_arn and set it from Vault via the deploy pipeline or use external data source that reads Secrets Manager. That keeps terraform immutable and rotation-friendly.
oliver: +1 to var.cert_arn. Also add a note in the module README about rotation and which team owns the cert. Makes audits easier.
endri: operational note: if you need both ALB and NLB to present the same cert, prefer central cert manager that updates k8s secret and an external cert_ref in terraform (data source). Otherwise you end up with drift.
sam: ok I'll update PR: switch to var.cert_arn and add docs pointer to cert sync. Also add RBAC for infra-cert namespace so svc accounts can mount when pods need TLS. Will tag @natalie for review.
li: one more: canary strategy — rolling to NLB first in staging, then enable cross-zone and health check on target group's port. For production, do a small traffic shift to ALB fallback then cutover.
natalie: sounds good. If you want I'll run the secret/RBAC changes after your module change is merged.
sam: thanks all. I'll push changes tonight. cc @oliver for README nit. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: plan completed (run-id: 4c2f) — 1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. Details: aws_lb.my-nlb (create), aws_lb_listener.my-nlb-listener (create), aws_lb_target_group.my-nlb-tg (create)
sam: noted. will follow up with a separate PR for Vault->k8s sync job.
